characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl family, increasing ferrite content with increasing Al content is more relevant for the mechanical trend than the presence of κ-carbides or ε-martensite.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling and water quenching resulted in a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction

characterization_methods.key_findings: For the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl family, yield strength and ultimate tensile strength both increase while tensile elongation drops as a function of Al content in the range 2–11 wt.% Al.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical property screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds were successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock; five different alloys were synthesized in one operation.
10×50×130 mm^3 blocks were hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2×60×55 mm^3 for each alloy composition.
Aging was one of the nine heat treatments (450/500/550/600 °C for 0 h, 1 h, and 24 h) applied after homogenization.
Performed after the heat treatments to remove surface scale.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

defects.porosity: none observed (no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials)

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure with a grain size of ~20 μm and some retained microsegregations of Mn; metallographic analysis showed no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials. For the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl family, XRD screening indicates that increasing ferrite content accompanies increasing Al content.

unmapped_findings: Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl family-level mechanical trend (b0026): yield strength and ultimate tensile strength both increase while tensile elongation drops as a function of Al content in the range 2–11 wt.% Al. This is a family-level trend and is not specific to the 500 °C/1 h aging condition of the present sample.

Figure 6 mechanical data for Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl are plotted for as-quenched, 400 °C 24 h, 500 °C 24 h, and 600 °C 24 h conditions (NOT the 500 °C/1 h condition of this sample). Example 24-h values: at ~10.5 wt.% Al, YS ≈ 690 MPa (500 °C), UTS ≈ 900 MPa (500 °C), tensile elongation ≈ 12–25%, hardness ≈ 290 HBW; tensile elongation peaks at ~80–85% near 2 wt.% Al.

Figure 6 XRD phase-fraction bar charts (24-h aging conditions) for Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl: the 2Al alloy is ~100 vol.% γ austenite; higher-Al alloys contain α ferrite; the highest-Al alloy develops κ-carbide at 600 °C; a small ε-martensite cap appears in one chart. These phase fractions correspond to the 24-h conditions, not the 500 °C/1 h sample.

General RAP processing context (b0020): aging at 450/500/550/600 °C for 0 h/1 h/24 h produces a matrix of 45 sample conditions; tensile tests were at room temperature with initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1, with values plotted as averages of three measurements per material state.
